overview.overview:
Nebraska's 2nd District, which awards a single electoral vote separately from the statewide winner, has become one of the most closely watched split districts in the country. It backed the Democratic presidential candidate in 2020 by 6.5 points and again in 2024 by 4.6 points, running several points ahead of the nation as a whole in both elections.

The forecast expects the Democratic nominee to carry the district by roughly 10 points, reflecting a favorable national environment layered on top of the district's existing Democratic lean. The 80 percent range runs from a narrow 0.3-point margin to a 19.7-point margin, so the district is expected to stay on one side of the ledger, though the size of the margin varies widely.
overview.watch: A substantially worse national environment for the Democratic nominee, or a shift in the Omaha-area suburbs toward Republicans, could bring the district back into single-digit competitive territory.
key_factors: The district's consistent Democratic lean of about 5 points relative to the nation
A favorable national environment of roughly 4.75 points for the Democratic nominee
The single electoral vote's limited influence, with tipping-point odds near zero
